commands.label: Generate actual TL serialization code and round-trip one value with Telethon

tl.py.content_utf8:
import sys, io, types, importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
from telethon_generator.parsers.tlobject import parse_tl
from telethon_generator.generators import tlobject
from telethon.extensions.binaryreader import BinaryReader
from telethon.tl.tlobject import TLObject
items=list(parse_tl(Path("hello.tl"),layer=0))
assert len(items)==1 and items[0].fullname=="corpus.greeting",items
out=Path("generated")
out.mkdir()
tlobject.generate_tlobjects(items, layer=0, import_depth=2, output_dir=out)
candidate=next(p for p in out.rglob("*.py") if "class Greeting(" in p.read_text())
text=candidate.read_text()
print(text)
import telethon.tl.types
m=types.ModuleType("telethon.tl.types.corpus_fixture")
m.__package__="telethon.tl.types"
exec(compile(text,str(candidate),"exec"),m.__dict__)
message=m.Greeting(text="Hello, World!")
wire=bytes(message)
with BinaryReader(wire) as read:
    assert read.read_int(signed=False)==m.Greeting.CONSTRUCTOR_ID
    actual=m.Greeting.from_reader(read)
    assert actual.text==message.text
print("TL_ROUNDTRIP="+actual.text)

reproduction_command: python tl.py with Telethon generator and runtime
semantic_scope: Telethon compiled the unchanged Telegram TL schema into its real serializer class, then wrote and read back the exact greeting with the correct constructor identifier.
